clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-671 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8483-exemption-louis-loebl-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed July 16, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts Louis Loebl from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, September 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of September 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when September 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8828, signed July 24, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("by Executive Order No. 8483 of July 16, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending September 30, 1942". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses. Cited EO 8828 APP abbreviates sec. 715a where GPO spells section 715a; same authority and operative grant. This is a nonmaterial abbreviation, not a changed legal proposition.
